text: The best part of Pushkar wasn't a place. It was one guy playing one string by the lake.
I could not stop trying to make the trip useful. Every walk felt like it needed to become a memory, a photo or a story.
That evening, walking past the ghats, a folk musician was playing. No amp, no crowd, just him, the lake and one string.
The instrument looked older than I was and somehow the whole place felt quieter. I just stood there, I wasn't filming or checking the time.
It was one of the few moments that whole trip where I stopped asking what I was getting out of it.
If you want the two questions I asked myself before every trip now, comment Pushkar, I'll send them over.
